118: Variables are rendered within the `{{ ... }}` expressions.
119: ```.cpp
120: json data;
121: data["neighbour"] = "Peter";
122: data["guests"] = {"Jeff", "Tom", "Patrick"};
123: data["time"]["start"] = 16;
124: data["time"]["end"] = 22;
125: 
126: // Indexing in array
127: render("{{ guests.1 }}", data); // "Tom"
128: 
129: // Objects
130: render("{{ time.start }} to {{ time.end + 1 }}pm", data); // "16 to 23pm"
131: ```
132: If no variable is found, valid JSON is printed directly, otherwise an `inja::RenderError` is thrown.
133: 
134: ### Statements
135: 
136: Statements can be written either with the `{% ... %}` syntax or the `##` syntax for entire lines. Note that `##` needs to start the line without indentation. The most important statements are loops, conditions and file includes. All statements can be nested.
